2028 Lincoln Navigator Refresh Comes From Behind the CGI Curtain, Shows All Goodies Inside and Out
25 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
The winners and losers of the latest US automotive sales reports include Mazda, Ram, Cadillac, Ford, Lincoln , Fiat, or Alfa Romeo. But which is which and who is who, plus what it does have to do with a CGI design project?
We’re into the final stretch for 2026 and so far, the automotive market has been just as convoluted as international relationships between various countries are right now. Over in America, Cadillac’s EV-heavy lineup suffered tremendously, with General Motors reporting its premium brand’s dip of 30% in the third quarter.
Concurrently, Ram jumped back into action and took over from Jeep during Q3 as the most popular brand from Stellantis, and it all has to do with the return of the Hemi V8, of course. Mazda’s ‘old cars’ like the MX-5 Miata and the Mazda3 jumped tremendously because they’re simply affordable during expensive times, while brands like Fiat or Alfa Romeo show that they don’t have any sense of direction.
Ford saw mixed results – it’s keeping the F-Series above the competition, but overall, its Q3 sales dropped while the Mustang continues to get back on the right track. Lincoln, meanwhile, dropped no less than 18% while other premium brands like Infiniti rose more than 20%, largely impacted by the phase-out of the Corsair, just as Ford took a nose-dive because it’s axing the Escape.
Soon, Lincoln is going to be left with only the Aviator, Nautilus, and the mighty Navigator. Of course, the latter remains an important halo model even though it can’t compare in terms of sales with the Nautilus. It also had the smallest gain across the past three months, up about three percent according to Ford Authority, while the Aviator is breathing down its neck with an 11% surge and the Nautilus is almost 18% up year-over-year.
No worries, as there are solutions – cue the rumor mill and the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. For example, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have unofficially imagined the CGI looks of the mid-cycle refresh for the Lincoln Navigator to make it enticing once again, especially against fresher models like the facelifted Cadillac Escalade or the all-new Infiniti QX80, among others.
The host of the channel believes that next year the 2028 Lincoln Navigator and the long wheelbase version could get a mid-cycle refresh procedure along the same styling coordinates as the 2027 Nautilus, complete with a front-end restyle, an update to the interior with a new steering wheel and larger central display, plus additional colors.
The channel’s resident virtual artist then takes over to present the changes in an unofficial, hypothetical design project – we see the ‘new’ and ‘old’ models side-by-side both inside and outside, as always. There is also a traditional color reel, of course. So, what do you think?

China's 2027 BMW i3 50L Electric Sedan Covers 753 Miles Without Recharging
9 photos
Photo: BMW
A distinct animal from the i3 for Europe and the United States of America, the i3 L that BMW produces in China stands out in a few choice ways. Not only does it have a longer wheelbase and way nicer pull-up door handles than its Western counterpart, but in the CLTC, the i3 L can handle over 1,000 kilometers (621 miles) in the CLTC.
BMW China's estimate was a bit conservative, though. A series-production example of the i3 50L ran 1,213 kilometers (753 miles) on a single charge through a mix of city streets, national roads, and highway, crossing the line with 1 percent state of charge left on the battery gauge. It's the longest one-charge run of any electric Bimmer yet, exceeding the iX3 50L's 1,030-km drive from August 2026.
Given that most electric vehicles never hit rated numbers in real-world conditions, how did BMW China do it? For starters, the CLTC is the friendliest measuring stick for battery-electric vehicles in the industry. But more importantly, endurance tests like this one are rarely conducted in actual real-world conditions, where traffic sucks the life out of you and the air con is on full blast most of the time.
The CLTC per se is problematic as well, for the passenger vehicle cycle adopted in October 2021 lasts exactly 1,800 seconds on a dynamometer. It covers a mere 14.5 kilometers (9 miles), averages 29 kilometers per hour (18 miles per hour), and speeds don't get higher than 114 kilometers per hour (71 miles per hour). Add the 22 percent idling ratio to the aforementioned, and you will understand why the CLTC is way more optimistic than WLTP and the EPA's way of testing range.
CLTC-P splits into three main phases, beginning with a slow one mimicking gridlocked city traffic, a medium one for flowing urban arteries, and a single fast phase. Due to the relatively low speed of 114 kph (71 mph), the high-speed phase is unrealistic when compared to the highway speed limits in Europe and the US.
Photo: BMW The slow and medium phases eat most of the run, and battery-electric vehicles are way more efficient when driving at slower speeds. Compare that to the WLTP's 131 kilometers per hour (81 miles per hour) or the EPA's procedure, which deflates the result by a 0.7 adjustment factor, and you will certainly understand why the China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle divides opinion this sharply.
Confirmed on the big screen at the 2026 Chengdu Auto Show BMW media event, and cited by Car News China, the i3 50L managed 8.8 kilowatt-hours per 100 kilometers during the 1,213-kilometer test. Its battery is produced with locally sourced cells, with BMW China estimating 113.4 kilowatt-hours total capacity.
Based on the Neue Klasse platform of the iX3 L, the i3 L also supports charging at 400 kilowatts due to an 800-volt electrical architecture. Capable of adding 400 clicks (248 miles) of driving range in 10 minutes on direct current, the i3 L for China is available with a dual-motor setup that mirrors the 463 horsepower and peak torque rating of the EU-market i3 50 xDrive.
BMW China hasn't disclosed the average speed recorded during the endurance test, nor the route, ambient temperature, climate control use, or how many kilometers of highway driving. Those variables understandably swing an EV's consumption dramatically, so those 8.8 kWh/100 km should be treated as a carefully staged demonstration rather than a real-world average.
Speaking of, the WLTP estimates for the i3 50 xDrive are 18.0 to 13.4 kilowatt -hours per 100 clicks. Based on that average consumption, the i3 50 xDrive for Europe is theoretically capable of 758 to 912 kilometers (417 to 567 miles). In the United States of America, the preliminary BMW -estimated range tops 467 miles (752 kilometers).

2027 Audi RS Q5 Sportback Gets Unveiled Sans Camouflage Via Highly Realistic Virtual Illustrations
7 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The premium German automaker from Ingolstadt, Audi , isn’t doing all too well – especially across the very important market of America. But they sure hope to change that with the new roster they have baking in the oven.
The US automotive market has thoroughly accepted BMW’s leadership – the Bavarian automaker continues to hold the throne of luxury sales during the third quarter of 2026, well ahead of its pursuers. The premium brand from Bavaria sold exactly 100k units during the past quarter in America, with deliveries up by 3.4% and a year-to-date total of 287,154 sales.
The gap versus Lexus continues to grow wider, while Mercedes-Benz ranked third from far behind, and the other Germans are going through tough times: Volkswagen, Audi, and Porsche all fell through the US automotive sales charts during the past quarter, with Porsche only sending 16k units to clients during the period and Audi contracting to less than 40k examples, down 13% and 15%, respectively.
Obviously, that’s a shameful performance for both, especially at Audi, where the year-to-date total has reached less than 108k units, sliding by 16% compared to the first nine months of last year. The Ingolstadt-based automaker has 15 active nameplates on sale in the US market, and only six of them had a positive performance during the past nine months.
The signs of improvement are shy, at the moment, with the new A5 and A6 rising fast by 21 and 24%, respectively, but they don’t occupy significant volume to help sway the negative performance. Luckily for Audi, the third-generation Q7 mid-size crossover SUV and the first-ever full-size three-row Q9 are coming soon and could provide a massive boom during 2027.
Knowing that, it’s no wonder that even the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators at time stop across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to focus on Audi. For example, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the new Audi RS Q5 – the first-ever Audi Sport model of the RS variety for the Q5 series have been spied recently by our spy photographer partners shedding more and more of the pesky camouflage.
As such, it’s easier now for the pixel master to peel off the remaining layers and provide us with realistic renderings. This time around, he’s focusing on the sportier Sportback model, showing off the muscular attire, complete with large wheels and a massive front fascia plus an ICE -intensive rear. Even better, the CGI expert also compares the imagined model with an actual foe – the Mercedes- AMG GLC Coupe. So, what do you think – do you have a new favorite or not? Tesla Just Broke the Internet With the New Roadster and I Think It's the Silliest Thing Yet
13 photos
Photo: Tesla
I just woke up, made coffee, and started scrolling my feed to see what happened while I was asleep. And it’s one particular thing that stands out the most, namely the new Tesla Roadster , which is the most talked-about thing by far. And it truly sounds impressive, but is it?
The internet refers to it as a flying car, stating that we just got flying cars before GTA VI. But did we? Actually, it does not fly, as all it does is break its fall mid-air. If the clips are true, and I seriously doubt that some of them are. And before you criticize me for refusing to see left and right, let’s not forget that we are in the AI (or SI as Trump likes to call it) era. And it’s a multi-billion company that we are talking about, so the resources are definitely there.
Second, Elon Musk has already made several promises that haven’t materialized. A quick search online shows that Level 5 fully autonomous vehicles and one million Robotaxis should have been on the road by 2020. Humans should have been on Mars by 2021, a date that then changed to 2024 and 2025. And we are in 2026 in case you forgot. Lunar tourism is another thing, and that should have happened in 2023. That’s three years ago, and we still do not have that.
Fully autonomous robots, the Hyperloop, DOGE, The Boring Company solving the problem of traffic jams, the removal of bots in X / Twitter, the Candy (Awesome) company, and the constant delay of new products are other things that need to be mentioned. And no, I’m not a Musk hater, I’m just here to point out the obvious.
Photo: Tesla On top of that, Elon has learned from the Tesla Cybertruck’s presentation, whose window shattered during a demonstration that was all about its ballistic prowess, so him and his PR army weren’t going to leave anything to chance when it came to the unveiling of the Roadster. Thus, everything went smooth, people were shocked, some still are, and others will be once they see the clips, but to me, it looks like another promise that won’t materialize. And I am really trying not to use the word “fake.”
Tesla’s famous delays have hit the new-generation Roadster (and not only) like a freight train. The model was unveiled as a concept back in 2017, and that’s nine years ago. The initial promise was that we would see it on the road in 2020. The original deadline was missed, and after that, Elon Musk claimed that it would come out in 2021, 2022, and 2023. In the latter year, he said that it will “hopefully” hit the assembly line in 2024. Then 2025 came, and now 2026, and this thing is still not fully ready.
But wait, hasn’t it just been uncovered ? Well, it was actually demonstrated, as this thing is still not ready. What you are looking at is a prototype, as now Musk claims that the new Tesla Roadster will enter production in 2028. And if I were to bet on it, I’d say that it probably won’t come out until the turn of the decade. And by then, the model would be 13 years old, as the original concept broke cover in 2017, as mentioned above.
Photo: Tesla Thus, it’s not exactly the world’s fastest production car, because it is not in production. It’s not a flying car either because it cannot fly. It just jumps, and looks fantastic while doing that, but I cannot imagine a single scenario in the real world where this would be safe. Imagine that the driver and passengers would have to be seriously strapped. There shouldn’t be any things that could fly in the cockpit during this trick, and let’s not forget that all it takes is a single sensor failing, and you have a catastrophe waiting to happen.
The new Tesla Roadster reportedly has fans underneath that provide up to 2Gs of downforce while this thing stands still. There are also 10 cold-gas thrusters that allow it to maneuver mid-air, fed by ultra-high-pressure air from a couple of 600-liter tanks that are onboard. These thrusters rocket (pun intended) the car to 60 mph (97 kph) in less than one second. The official number is 0.81 seconds, according to the company.
Everything sounds cool, but launching a car equipped with thrusters that can jump and break its fall is definitely a headache, not to mention anything but safe, and while the Tesla fanboys will likely criticize me for what I’ve said here, I do not believe that something like this will hit the road in full production guise.
It’s likely that Musk’s company will let its fans forget about it for a few years, and when the new Roadster finally debuts and goes on sale, he will probably blame the lack of thrusters on something such as the legislation, huge delays, the supplier chain, or something like that. Thus, what we have here is a very clever marketing stunt that’s bound to keep people talking about it for days, weeks, months, and years to come. Car Nut Got 1968 Charger R/T "Family Car," Bounced 8 States in 32 Years, Broadcast Sheet Still in It
49 photos
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150
Cars staying with one owner, or one family for decades are not unusual. But a car that moves around through eight of the 48 contiguous states of the Union is not something you hear about from your local Amazon delivery guy every week. Or ever. so picture the amazement of this Moparhead when said owners of said car reached out to aske if he’d buy it. Did I mention it’s a numbers-matching 1968 Dodge Charger R/T?
The story begins in 1994 (for some of use, that’s two holidays ago), when a gearhead named Mark found himself home alone in Sacramento, California, during a weekend. The man’s wife together with their two kids left to visit her mother (Mark’s in-law), leaving the man unbothered to solve a simple task he’d been postponing for years: find a good driver car.
Mark already possessed a rocky history with Chrysler products, having previously owned a 1967 Dodge Charger fastback that stranded his wife almost every time she drove it until he finally parted ways with that temperamental machine in the mid-1980s. Mopar ownership experience in a nutshell – back when most Dodge Chargers were simply winter beaters, grocery-getter, dime-a-dozen basket cases that were only marginally good as teen’s first cars.
Browsing the classic car classified ads in the Sacramento Bee newspaper, Mark narrowed his search down to two candidates: a 1979 Ford Mustang hatchback driven gently by an older woman (the ideal candidate) and a 1968 Dodge Charger R/T that had been drag raced. After taking out a high-interest cash advance on his credit card, he still stood $1,000 short of the asking price for the 10-year-newer Mustang and $750 below the seller's asking price for the Dodge.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 His prior experience with Dodge Chargers had left an indelible impression on the family man, who was now a responsible adult with enough sense to make a mature decision for his family. So of course he went all in on the muscle car, leaving the old lady’s fox-body pony Ford for someone else to enjoy. Why live bother-free, when you can always have weekly domestic tornado over a life-altering decision?
Choosing raw horsepower over daily practicality, Mark visited the Charger first and met the owner's father, who was selling the former drag racer to fund his son's medical treatment in a rehabilitation facility. Mark offered every single dollar of borrowed cash he held in his hands. The seller accepted the deal, and Mark drove the big-block muscle car home feeling untouchable, only to find out that you can, in fact, camp indoors, only it’s called “sleeping on the couch.”
At the time of the purchase, Mark worked on the morning broadcast for a Sacramento rock radio station and quickly convinced the station and its commercial advertisers to sponsor a mechanical refresh adventure.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 Through those local promotional partnerships, he rebuilt crucial components of the Charger's 440-cubic-inch Magnum V8 engine. He initially dreamed of executing a full factory-correct restoration, but time and finances transformed the muscle car into a rolling project.
Over the next 26 years, as Mark transitioned into a career in law enforcement and served as a state park warden near El Vado Lake in New Mexico, the Charger followed him nationwide. The Dodge was trailered through California, New Jersey, Texas, New Mexico, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Vermont. On every move, Mark assured transport drivers the engine would start once the negative battery terminal was connected, yet it never fired up.
While garaging the coupe in Vermont, Mark fired up the big-block a few times each year and changed its motor oil every other year, but he eventually accepted that he would never complete the project. In 2020, before retiring to San Antonio, he passed the Charger to Margaret, his daughter, and Jared, her husband, so it would stay in the family. The couple promptly loaded the classic Mopar onto a trailer and hauled it to Florida.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 Without a personal garage in Florida during their years-and-a-half stay, the couple rented a secure storage unit to shield the Charger from the elements. On weekends, they visited the unit, fired up the 440 V8, took short drives, occasionally smoked the rear tires, and spent hours browsing YearOne and JEGS restoration catalogs. Even while trailering the car to three successive homes across Texas, crowds gathered around it at every fuel stop.
With an upcoming move to Idaho and a later relocation to Northern California on the horizon, Margaret and Jared recognized their weekend routines left no bandwidth for an extensive rebuild. (At this time, I’m beginning to wonder if “Wander” is first nature in this family, or they just can’t grow roots deep enough in one place).
So, they made the reasonable decision: let it go to someone who can actually take care of it. it probably wasn’t as easy as it sounds, given the emotional connection to the car's XS29 VIN stamping. This Charger R/T was assembled at the Hamtramck plant in Michigan near where Margaret's family once resided and where Jared graduated from Wayne State University.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 There are quite a few Texas-based classic car dealerships that would have taken the car off them with both hands, but the couple didn’t just shoot in the dark. They reached out to Mopars5150, after a careful study of alternative. It doesn’t take a rocket science degree to determine that a 1968 Charger R/T with its original engine and transmission will automatically trigger the DEFCON 1 alert level on the YouTubing gearheads. Particularly when they learned the car was just an hour’s drive away.
Arriving at the property, Tony Sedillo inspected the remarkably solid California sheet metal. While the exterior wears weathered paint, a thick blanket of dust, and a replacement hood taken from a yellow donor car, the underside of the trunk lid displays its original factory E1 dark blue finish. Years prior to 1994, an earlier owner filled the circular 1968 side marker lights, installed an alarm cylinder on the fender, and added 1969 rear quarter emblems.
Inside the non-air-conditioned interior, factory bucket seats sit under aftermarket covers alongside a column-shifted 3-speed TorqueFlite automatic, a dashboard clock, and the outboard dash speakers of a rare factory 8-track radio setup. Although the original fender tag disappeared before Mark bought the car, he preserved every factory component he ever unbolted, boxing up the original drums after completing an aftermarket front disc brake conversion to make the Charger safer.
Photo: YouTube/Mopars5150 The previous owner who drag-raced this old classic wanted to perform a 4-speed swap, but fortunately never got to it, and the long-time errant caretaker who got it in ’94 was adamant on keeping it just as it left the assembly line, with its column shifter in place.
After four attempts, the engine fired up, so the YouTuber drove it on the trailer – that’s always a good sign for an old Mopar, and a great thing to have on an iconic muscle car like the 1968 Dodge Charger, the model that propelled the moniker into stardom. The emblematic round taillights and the concealed front lamps made history when they appeared on September 25, 1967, and became downright legendary on October 17, 1968, when “Bullitt” had its first public screening.
The second-generation Charger was allowed into the Road/Track family (established by the Coronet a year before), and it took full advantage of its birth rights. Out of the 96,000+ cars sold, 17,600 were R/Ts. The vast majority came in the standard configuration: 440-4 Magnum V8 (17,109 examples, 14,366 of which were 3-speed Torqueflite automatics), while the 426 Hemi motor was installed in 475 Chargers.
Tony Sedillo, the Mopars5150 know-it-all, went through the car and found the broadcast sheet in the rear seat, confirming that this is what it says it is. If you’re on the lookout for a project Mopar, this car will be available through their Celeste, Texas, showroom.

2027 BMW F 450 RR Is Like a Mini S 1000 RR, Cheaper Than Therapy
44 photos
Photo: BMW
It’s almost EICMA time and, as arguably the largest motorcycle show in the world is approaching, bike makers around the world are waking up following the slow summer months. So did BMW this week, which presented to the world something that’s basically a mini S 1000 RR, available at a fraction of the cost.
The name of the new motorcycle is F 450 RR , and it launches in the U.S. as a 2027 model year ride that’s set to become the entry-level machine in BMW’s supersport bikes portfolio, in all the ways that matter, from performance levels to cost.
The bike was constructed by the Bavarians around a welded tubular steel space-frame selected to provide the required rigidity. The chassis incorporates forged components, with the engine included in the design as a load-bearing element.
Speaking of that, the motorcycle is animated by a liquid-cooled 420cc parallel-twin engine with a 72 mm bore and 51.6 mm stroke. It’s the unit that has already been introduced on the BMW F 450 GS, only reengineered to suit the needs of a supersport.
The performance numbers of the transversely mounted piece of hardware are exactly what you’d expect from an entry-level machine: 48 hp at 8,750 rpm and 32 lb.-ft. of torque at 6,750 rpm. These translate into an acceleration time from standstill to 62 mph of 5.6 seconds, and a top speed of 110 mph (177 kph).
Photo: BMW Motorrad A stainless-steel exhaust system helps it breathe, and the German bike maker’s Easy Ride Clutch can be on deck to allow riders to enjoy their trip without using the clutch lever. Another component of the drivetrain is the six-speed transmission that sends torque to the left-side secondary drive. The unit comes with a reversible shift pattern suited for use on the track.
The motorcycle can be set to operate in one of three main modes, namely Rain, Road, and Race. A series of assistance features are on deck to help riders along, including ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), and Dynamic Traction Control (DTC).
BMW Motorrad didn’t cut corners when it comes to the suspension setup either, and it chose KYB components. The company went for an upside-down telescopic fork at the front, adjustable for compression and rebound, and an aluminum hollow-cast double-sided swingarm with a central spring shock at the rear, it too adjustable for spring preload and rebound damping.
Overall, the bike comes with suspension travel of 5.5 inches. These elements tie into cast-aluminum 17-inch wheels with hollow spokes at both ends. Brembo braking hardware is on deck to supply stopping power.
Photo: BMW Motorrad Elsewhere, the 2027 BMW F 450 RR deploys forged-aluminum foot controls and side stand, heated grips right off the factory floor, and footpeg brackets for the passenger that are bolted directly to the frame.
Last but not least, the motorcycle ships as stock with full LED lights, a 6.5-inch TFT display that allows smartphone connectivity, and a USB-C charging point for the rider’s handheld devices.
When it comes to the overall design, the F 450 RR borrows a lot from its bigger S 1000 RR sibling, including the nose-down/tail-down appearance, the fly line, and winglets. Why, it even comes with an asymmetrical side fairing panel, complete with the telltale gills.
Up on the frame, BMW installed a 3.69-gallon (14 liters) fuel tank, and behind that a two-piece seat that floats 31.1 inches (790 mm) off the ground. The tail section includes discreetly placed grab handles.
The new addition to the BMW supersport motorcycle family may have been presented this week, but it will take a long time to reach the U.S. - the local market won’t see the model become available until the summer of 2027.
Photo: BMW Motorrad There will be only one variant available, the M Sport, in a single color choice, Snaefell White / M Motorsport. That means a white frame with wheel decals in the M Motorsport colors, but also that the red version you see in the attached gallery won’t be sold, at least for now, on the American market.
I said earlier that the 2027 BMW F 450 RR is cheaper than therapy, and it’s about time to reveal what that means. BMW settled on an MSRP of $7,815, making the ride one of the most affordable machines available at the time of writing in BMW’s portfolio.
That, of course, is only the starting price, as a lot of extras are on the table, including the $330 Innovation Package, soft cases capable of holding 16.5 liters of stuff, a tank bag , roll bags going from 40 to 60 liters, and so on.
BMW didn’t specifically say that it will bring the F 450 RR to the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan, Italy, early next month, but there’s a good chance it will. autoevolution will be on location to bring you all the hot stories from there.

source_document.body:
PERTH, Australia — An Australian startup is developing new tactical orchestration software that will allow Boxer 8x8 armored vehicles to control unmanned systems in the air and on the ground simply by operators giving verbal instructions.
Sydney-based Breaker Industries, founded three years ago, is working with Rheinmetall Defence Australia to perfect the Avalon human-machine interface that will make a Boxer commander’s duties less onerous in the heat of combat.
The two firms signed a teaming agreement on Oct. 6, the opening day of the Land Forces 2026 exhibition in Perth. Work will now continue for twelve months to mature the Avalon system for the Boxer, including trials slated for mid-2027.
Michael Irwin, co-founder of Breaker, demonstrated to Defense News how simple voice commands – using the same type of language for directing soldiers – can control drones and get them to perform various tasks.
With uncrewed systems proliferating on battlefields, Irwin said, “The goal is to allow an armored vehicle crew to easily work with teams of those autonomous systems like they were working with another crew member.”
Indeed, he described the software stack as simply a “digital crew member.” Instead of having several extra soldiers dedicated to drone operation taking up space in the rear of the Boxer, this software helps the commander marshal all the assets in the proverbial toolbox.
The Australian Army is acquiring 211 Boxers, with production currently underway at Rheinmetall’s facility near Brisbane. These vehicles are used by cavalry units, so the smooth integration of drones could help enhance the soldiers’ ability to see around the next corner or over the next hill.
Rheinmetall described the software as enabling a “step change in armored vehicle operations capability.”
This system was demonstrated within six months of the project being launched. That demonstration involved a soldier with less than 30 minutes of training controlling a swarm of drones through the Boxer’s standard headset and microphone. They did so while performing normal crew commander functions.
Breaker chose the Boxer as the launch platform because of its digitized backbone, and the Australian Army is “very keen to see it developed,” according to company representatives.
Irwin believes the system is applicable to other vehicles in the Australian Army too, including Hanwha’s AS21 Redback infantry fighting vehicle, due to enter service soon.
The future adoption of Breaker's Avalon software will enable Boxer crews to command drones outside their vehicles via voice commands. (Gordon Arthur)
Nathan Poyner, managing director of Rheinmetall Defence Australia, said there is “most definitely” an opportunity to add this Avalon system to other Boxer users in Europe.
Irwin believes one day a Boxer or other armored vehicle itself could be controlled by voice. For example, the turret could be asked to keep watch on a particular arc.
“It’s technically feasible, but there’s a whole lot of cultural barriers to get through” before this level of autonomy can happen, Irwin said.
Notably, Rheinmetall Australia is manufacturing Boxers fitted with a Lance turret and 30 mm cannon for the German Army. The company won a contract to deliver these heavy weapon carriers to Germany, with the Bundeswehr following the same configuration selected by the Australian Army.
Australia received the first 25 Boxer Block 1 vehicles from Rheinmetall Germany, but the remaining Block 2 vehicles were designed and are being manufactured in Australia.
There are six unique Boxer variants destined to join the Australian Army, and Poyner said five have completed their development so far.
He added that more than 50% of the Boxer’s content is manufactured in Australia, an indication of the depth of the supply chain that Rheinmetall has achieved Down Under.
Poyner added that he is in talks with the Australian military about additional variants of the Boxer, with a counter-drone and air-defense variant armed with a Skyranger 30 turret, made by Rheinmetall’s Switzerland offshoot, considered the most suitable.
About Gordon Arthur
Gordon Arthur is an Asia correspondent for Defense News. After a 20-year stint working in Hong Kong, he now resides in New Zealand. He has attended military exercises and defense exhibitions in about 20 countries around the Asia-Pacific region.

Your Next BMW Will Be Made by AI and This Could Get Very Wrong
20 photos
Photo: BMW AG
In the fall of 2026, BMW dropped a bombshell that didn’t quite send the shockwaves it should have throughout the automotive industry, and that’s probably because it was firstly presented to its shareholders, and secondly because it was dressed as a brilliant cost-saving measure for the future.
Before jumping into the following diatribe, I should probably first present the facts in the way that they were presented by BMW itself in a press release at the end of September, 2026. In short, the main story was centered about a restructuring program that was announced at BMW Group’s Capital Market Day, which is nothing out of the ordinary in this day and age, when “cost-cutting,” “spiralling market share” and “falling profits” are some of the most used expressions in any automotive corporate meeting in Germany.
What was out of the ordinary was the rest of the context, as BMW pretty much announced that it will even integrate AI into its corporate ladder. The German carmaker has been integrating AI deep into its production and various other parts of its organization since 2023, and has been using AI agents tasked with monitoring geopolitical risks, product quality and cutting costs for some time now. That said, they are truly going for it on a whole other level in the near future.
With the latest measures, set to be implemented during 2027 and completed until 2028, the Munich carmaker is set to reduce the number of divisions and associated management roles by 20 percent . These positions will not disappear into thin air, though, at least not exactly. as they will be replaced by a large-scale deployment of “agentic AI applications.”
These software agents are allegedly capable of performing a bunch of tasks with minimal human intervention, and will be in charge of various things, including, and this is where the bombshell comes, development, purchasing from suppliers, sales and aftersales. BMW calls it a game-changer in the automotive industry, and I fully agree.
Believe it or not, by 2028 BMW is set to become more of an “AI-orchestrated company” than any other car automaker out there. The main idea is to reduce costs, albeit it’s not exclusively doing that, and Munich expects to reach approximately 1 billion euros in annual savings by 2028, an interim EBIT margin of 3 to 5 percent and a return to the long-term 8 to 10 percent target range by the start of 2030, and it’s all thanks to this deployment of AI.
Now, what BMW has not mentioned is which specific decisions these agentic AI systems will be making, how they will be validated, what happens when (not if) they are wrong, and who will be held accountable for the consequences of their errors. On top of it, it’s not clear how the carmaker will manage the transition from a management structure designed around human judgement to one designed around algorithmic recommendations or decisions.
I think these are all perfectly suitable questions that should have been answered before all the shareholders were informed of the plan. I’m not saying it’s an awful plan, but its complexity and never-before-seen scale deserve a much closer look. BMW told everyone the upsides, but maybe we should look at the potential downsides as well, since from some perspectives it sounds awfully close to opening a Pandora’s box.
The Decision Rights Problem and the Lack of Accountability One of the most important issues that need clarification for a better understanding of the plan is who owns the sign-off for a decision made largely or in totality by AI. Before, the management structure of BMW and pretty much every single large corporation included management layers, with each one bearing total responsibility for their individual decisions.
BMW does note that people still make the final decision in its current phase of using agentic AI systems for recommendations, as AI is not autonomous. The 20 percent management reduction and its replacement with AI suggests that the human beings who currently own the sign-off will no longer be employed when those decisions need to be made.
Photo: BMW AG During my time documenting for this article I learned more than I would have wanted about how big corporations work, and about business in general. This definitely allowed me to have a better viewpoint about what BMW is doing. In layman terms, if the AI is not making the decisions autonomously and the human who made them is no longer around, the decision right is orphaned. That expression existed long before the rise of AI, and it traditionally revolved around the world of copyright, where “orphaned work” was something for which the rightholders could not be determined or were no longer contactable.
You can probably see the resemblance with replacing human executives with AI in Munich. Moving on, I also learned about the terms RACI and RAPID, which are used by most successful corporations. RACI apparently stands for Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed, and it is a framework or chain of approval used by project managers for day-to-day project execution and routine tasks.
RAPID stands for Recommend, Agree, Perform, Input, and Decide, and is used by executives for more complex decision-making instead of routine tasks. In their own ways, both models pretty much explain who does the work, who is advisor, who gets updated, and last but not least, who holds the ultimate authority. It’s unclear how or if BMW will use any of the two models after AI replaces those humans.
This is one of the reasons why BMW’s reorganization and the inevitable appearance of “orphaned decision rights” feels like opening a Pandora’s box. The carmaker does say that when it comes to vehicle development, all the results given by AI are monitored, reviewed and approved by the developers. In case it wasn’t obvious, AI has been assisting BMW in car development for a while now, thanks to the ongoing collaboration with Mistral AI, the largest European AI company.
In other words, when talking about the recent past and the present, every AI output that is used for various tasks is just an augmentation of a human reviewer. In the context of that 20 percent reduction in decision-making departments, a paradigm shift like this can birth a ton of consequences that can potentially be measured in billions and years of financial pain instead of enhancing profits.
Normally, when a human manager makes a terribly wrong decision, such as approving a supplier that fails or that the market rejects, or authorizes a cost reduction that compromises quality, the chain of accountability consequences are pretty clear. There is a clear decision trail, followed by a performance review and whatever leads from that.
Photo: BMW AG This is a normal and simple accountability structure that exists in just about every company, and it’s not about finding a scapegoat but more about giving every decision-maker a personal stake, incentivizing them not to make too many mistakes and accepting responsibility. An agentic AI system doesn’t have an incentive for anything, since it doesn’t have a career or a reputation to protect, a family to support, and not even a performance review or a pay cut to expect.
The AI, at least in its current form, is only optimized for the function it is given, using the data it has been trained on. In other words, it has no motivation to do anything, unlike a real human being whose name is on the decision. This fundamental difference between AI optimization and human accountability will always exist.
The question is what happens when one of BMW’s agentic AI systems makes a costly error, and who is legally and also professionally responsible. How will BMW even distinguish between an AI mistake that the AI itself clearly doesn’t define as one, because it falls within its trained parameters of an error, and one that happened because of poor training? These two questions, and others like them, definitely need to be addressed before those managers that currently own those responsibilities get their severance packages and are escorted out of the building.
The Human Cost and the Future Aspect BMW does note that it has reached an agreement with its Works Council to offer a severance package program for up to 8,000 people not involved in production , which would need to exit the building by the middle of 2027. Out of those, about 100 are executive positions that will be directly replaced by AI.
Obviously the financial aspect and the immediate economies of scale resulting from this move are extremely important for both BMW and the remaining workforce, whether they are part of the management or not. In fact, the voluntary severance program was sent a few days ago to approximately 40,000 workers, and the potential numbers made them so curious that they managed to render the company’s HR portal useless for a few hours during launch day.
Photo: BMW AG Tens of thousands of employees tried to access their individual offers almost simultaneously, and the servers simply couldn’t manage that much traffic at one time. The system was back online quickly, and normally this would be just a slightly amusing piece of news. In the context of some of those workers soon being replaced by AI, which needs tons of servers and high-speed bandwidth, maybe it’s less amusing and more food for thought.
Is BMW really ready to become an AI-archestrated car company when it can’t even provide enough servers and bandwidth for its internal e-mails to be checked at the same time? This is a huge bet on avant-garde technology that may or may not work as intended from the get-go, and the potential risks even with everything going smoothly on the backend are massive.
Now, don’t get me wrong, I get all the benefits, and BMW is not even the only giant company that already uses AI and plans to integrate it even more in its operations. Apart from customer service, which pretty much everyone has switched to AI, the shipping company has integrated artificial intelligence and machine learning to things like logistics, route planning and even customs operations. Even Bayer, the pharmaceutical company, uses AI to discover new drug compounds or conduct clinical trials.
So, why am I stressing so much about BMW getting on the AI bandwagon? Well, I wouldn’t have if BMW had stopped at using it only for optimizing some processes and improving their workflow, and therefore its profits. I’m not even disputing that the billion euros they are planning to get in annual savings isn’t a meaningful contribution to any German carmaker’s current dire financial situation.
What I am disputing is the clarity of BMW’s current plans and the accountability structure, because the official plan seems pretty much cobbled together from a low-level TED talk. What I’m also disputing is the amount of trust Munich seems to be putting in current AI technology. As I’m sure most of you know, in the vast majority of times, an AI simply works better than any human at a job it’s been trained in. Put it i n a robot and you no longer need physical work either, right?
But there are also times, more frequently than anyone enjoys, when AI systems simply hallucinate. When that happens (and it does, and will), the repercussions are more than just who gets the blame, but they may even trickle down to the end product. What I’m saying is that BMW opens up the possibility for a future batch of its cars to have a terrible defect that resulted from one of the AI agents that helped make it.
Last, but definitely not least, BMW went as far as calling some of these agentic AI systems “colleagues,” which sounds funny until it becomes more serious than anyone would want it. The remaining humans who will get to collaborate or even listen to orders from these “colleagues” will need to remember that AI technology is a tool, no matter how quicker than you it can access information. Mistaking a tool for a colleague might be the biggest risk that BMW is taking in this whole AI integration bet, or gamble, as I like to call it.

2026 Paris Motor Show • Denza Launching "God's Eye" Driving Assistance in Europe, the Z9GT Will Get It First
Tesla’s New Roadster Is a Real Stuntcar, Do You Like It More in Red? (Rendering)
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | theottle
Everyone and their pet are talking about the all-new Tesla Roadster today, because it is the thing that pretty much broke the internet. You have likely seen it already, found out what it is capable of, on paper, anyway, and watched the videos that show it in action.
So, what is this story all about then? Well, it’s not only those who reshare the clips on social media that want a small chunk of the viral pie, as so does the rendering crowd. One of the first virtual takes on this model after the official unveiling can be seen in the photo gallery above, and embedded at the bottom of this story, and it came from @theottle on Instagram.
If you are familiar with this rendering artist’s work, then you know that he tends to keep things realistic. And he wasn’t going to pull a different stunt in this case, because the all-new Tesla Roadster has had its pixels rearranged in order to wear a new color. It’s glossy red, and it is joined by the usual black accents on the lower parts of the body. The wheels carry over from the real thing, and the thrusters are visible at the rear.
Thus, this is a simply CGI take on the model that imagines it in a different color, and to be honest it does not look bad at all. However, we will probably have to wait two more years before we will see it dressed in a similar color, because it is bound to hit the assembly line in 2028. That’s what Elon Musk claimed, anyway, and given that we know how Tesla rolls, we wouldn’t hold our breath for it. Not in 2028, anyway.
Photo: Instagram | theottle In case you forgot, the new Tesla Roadster was supposed to hit the assembly line back in 2020. That was six years ago. Clearly, the deadline was missed, and after that, Musk promised that the electric hypercar will hit the road in 2021, in 2022, and in 2023. And in 2023, it said that it will “hopefully” hit production in 2024. That didn’t happen either, and now we are in 2026, and the model is still not ready to arrive at dealers.
Far from it, actually, because the vehicle that you have seen in the official photos and videos, and the countless clips shared on social media recently, is nothing more than a prototype. Still, it is one that looks quite cool, in the official demonstration, anyway, and it has been modified from the concept seen back in 2017, as it is now a lot more angular, and some say that it looks like a mix between the Tesla Cybertruck and a supercar from a few years ago. And that’s not exactly a bad thing, is it?
Tesla decided to call this model the Roadster, as you already know, just like the original model made between 2008 and 2012, which was reengineered Lotus Elise. And we suspected that it would be named that, though some outlets bet on different monikers, such as the CyberRoadster, or the Roadster 2.0, among others.
Photo: Instagram | theottle Now, the new Tesla Roadster has finally been demonstrated after further delays, proving that it is capable of pulling some jaw-dropping stunts, like jumping over various obstacles, and then breaking its fall. The automaker claims that it features fans underneath the provide 2Gs of downforce while the car stands still. On top of that, it also boasts no fewer than 10 cold-gas thrusters. These allow it to maneuver mid-air, and they are fed by a pair of 600-liter ultra-high-pressure air tanks that are on deck.
Elon Musk claimed that this is simply atmospheric air, so the tanks can be replenished on their own while the vehicle is being driven. These thrusters also turn the new Tesla Roadster into a veritable rocket, which takes a neck-snapping 0.81 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from rest. That’s what the company claims, anyway, though let’s not forget that this thing is still a prototype, and it will hit the road two years from now in the most realistic scenario, though we wouldn’t hold our breath for that debut date to be honest.
You see, despite the impressive demonstration that has taken the World Wide Web by storm, the Tesla Roadster hasn’t been detailed. Thus, we do not know how much power it has, what wheels are being driven (it’s probably all four, though) what the battery capacity is, how far it can travel, what is the production capacity, where it will be made, where it will launch initially, and other such details.
The official website reveals that the new Tesla Roadster will be offered in three trim levels. These will be called the Performance, Thrust, and Rocket, and it’s the mid-spec that can supposedly hit 60 mph in less than one second, and this one costs $250,000. The model that can fly is an “Invite Only,” and it is a single-seat version, by the looks of it. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Theo throttle – the fudger (@theottle)

Seven Generations of Ducati Superbikes Led to the New 2027 Panigale V4
8 photos
Photo: Ducati
When a new version of an existing motorcycle comes along, the world expects significant modifications in all departments. Yet, what Italian bike maker Ducati did with the 2027 Panigale V4 is proof that even the most minuscule of changes can have a huge impact on performance.
Building on the model that was introduced in the summer of 2024 as the 2025 model year, the Italians went all in to give the 2027MY more power, improved track times, and higher speeds. And they did that without going macro on the two-wheeler.
The main focus of the changes was the bike’s 1,103cc Desmosedici Stradale engine, which suffered targeted improvements that ended up modifying top power levels from 216 hp to 218 hp at 13,500 rpm.
That may not seem like much on paper, but in the real world it translates into 0.4 seconds gained per lap at the Vallelunga circuit during testing – and that could mean the difference between winning or losing a race. The most important changes implemented by Ducati were performed on the exhaust and lubrication systems.
On top of that, Ducati says it has improved high-RPM performance, and as a result of that, it raised the max RPM to 15,000 (up by 500 rpm) in gears from the second to the fifth. A longer final gearing was adopted, and the number of gear changes needed per lap has dropped by two.
Photo: Ducati Just like with the previous version, it is possible to take power levels even higher, by 11 hp and seven Nm of torque. That can be achieved by going for the Akrapovic exhaust system that can be installed as an option, a move that also drops the total weight of the motorcycle by 15 pounds (6.6 kg).
The frame of the Panigale V4 was not left to chance either, as, in its race to make the motorcycle faster and better, it ended up making the chassis less stiff than before and capable of taking higher mid-corner speed.
Targeting the front part of the frame, the upgrades have resulted in a 12 percent reduction in lateral stiffness. This, in turn, cascades into increased front-end grip, more precise feel during turn-in, and an improved ability to tighten the line heading into the apex.
Ducati dived into the bike’s electronics package as well, and added a new feature called the Dynamic Engine Brake. Replacing the previous Engine Brake Control, it modulates braking based on the actual load on the rear tire to provide greater stability when slowing down at lean angles.
Photo: Ducati Another technological debut on the 2027 Panigale V4 is the Race Brake Control, which is meant to increase the rear wheel’s contribution to braking power and allow for the available grip to be properly exploited.
Ducati modified a number of other components of the motorcycle, including by introducing new adjustable clip-on handlebars specifically tailored for track use and raised by ten mm to follow what’s happening in MotoGP.
Other than that, the Panigale V4 retains its curb weight of 412 pounds (187 kg), and continues to be offered with forged aluminum wheels shod in Pirelli Diablo Supercorsa V4 tires. The suspension system that ties into them, of the Ohlins variety, seems to have remained unchanged.
At the beginning of the year, the Italian bike maker launched something called the Ducati Factory Made. By trade, that’s a factory-backed customization program that gives customers the option of configuring rides to their own liking right off the factory floor.
Photo: Ducati As of now, for the first time, the S version of the new Panigale is joining the Factory Made program, giving buyers access to a choice of 11 body colors (five of which come directly from Lamborghini's Ad Personam program), two distinct liveries (Corse and Performance), and a pretty large number of accessories that can be installed right on the assembly lines.
The list includes, among others, the Pro and Pro+ versions of the Front Brake system, the STM dry clutch, and adjustable footpegs.
Ducati says the new Panigale V4, which is the culmination of a bloodline that stretches back seven generations, will be available at European dealers starting March of next year, and we expect the U.S. launch to happen shortly after that, in April 2027, with the rest of the world to follow.
There is no word on how much the motorcycle will cost yet, but the current version of the two-wheeler sells in America for prices that start at around $28,000. The bike comes from the factory floor as a single-seater, but there is the option of installing a passenger kit.
In a couple of weeks, the largest moto show in the world, the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA), opens its doors in Milan, Italy, and, even if Ducati didn’t confirm the new Panigale V4 will be there, we’ll keep an eye on things to see if we can spot it in the metal.
